doc.title: Joe Wilder Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Moving to New York and Marine Corps service at Montford Point
summary: He has lived in New York since 1947; in the Marines he was Assistant Bandmaster at Montford Point, then returned to Hampton briefly and left for Lunceford.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Oh, boy. Have you lived in New York most of your life?

I guess yes I have as a matter of fact, since 1947. I was born in Colwyn, Pennsylvania though. And I went into the Marine Corps for three years and when I came out I went back with Lionel Hampton and I stayed there a short time and I wasn’t very happy and I left that band and went with Jimmy Lunceford.
Were you able to play in the service?

Yeah, I was the Assistant Bandmaster at Montford Point Marine Base. My platoon, as a matter of fact, this was one of the first times they had black Marines. And my platoon brought the number of black Marines to ten hundred, the first ten hundred black Marines.
Most of the musicians we’ve talked to who were in the service, were able to play music.
Most of them were, yeah. But we took regular Basic Training too, so that we were always being reminded that you are in the band but you’re in the Marine Corps too you know.
